findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a publicly resolvable endpoint reachable from the internet rather than confining it to the VPC. Combined with an admin password supplied through a Terraform variable, this exposes the database directly to credential-guessing and exploitation of any MySQL vulnerability from untrusted networks.

storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volumes, automated snapshots and backups, so all catalog data (including the EMPLOYEES PII table created by the app) is written to disk in cleartext.

The master user is the well-known default 'admin' and its password is supplied from var.password, a plain Terraform variable that will be stored in cleartext in state and is reused verbatim in EC2 user data. A predictable admin account on an internet-reachable endpoint materially lowers the cost of a credential attack.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password directly into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext by any process or SSRF-capable request that can reach the instance metadata service, and it is also visible via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the database master credentials.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the internet-facing web server. Compromise of the web tier yields full read/write/delete over every bucket, instance and database in the account, including snapshot exfiltration and security-group modification; ec2:* also enables lateral movement and network-boundary changes.

No metadata_options block is specified, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (token-optional). A server-side request forgery in the hand-written PHP application would let an attacker retrieve the over-privileged role's temporary credentials and the plaintext user-data secrets without any token challenge.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume - which persists /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc containing the database master password - may be stored unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption happens to be enabled.

The bootstrap installs and starts httpd serving the form-based application over plain HTTP with no TLS certificate or HTTPS listener, and the public DNS name is exported as an output. Submitted employee names and addresses, and any session data, traverse the network in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, while the application connects with mysqli_connect() without SSL options. Database credentials and query results therefore cross the network unencrypted.

Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR instead of being restricted to the application server's security group, so every workload in the VPC - including any future untrusted or compromised subnet resident - can attempt to reach the database.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0. A database tier has no need for unrestricted internet egress, and this path facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control following a successful exploit.
